subject: Post-signature MAP: staged rollout, canary & training schedule (HelioMatrix)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lewis <sara@heliomatrix.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature MAP: staged rollout, canary & training schedule (HelioMatrix)

Sara — thanks again for signing. I promised a concrete MAP that bundles rollout windows, canary gating, migration cutover, and the training plan for your support and engineering teams. Draft attached (heliomatrix_map_v1.xlsx) — high level sections below:

- Week 0 (Prep): account provisioning, KMS & VPC checks, baseline performance eval
- Week 1 (Canary A): limited traffic to Canary 1 (10% traffic), KV cache priming, observability hooks
- Week 2 (Canary B): broader canary (40%), run regression prompt set and latency/quality evals
- Week 3 (Migration): full cutover window (low traffic), rollback plan rehearsed
- Training & Handover: two 90-minute sessions (Engineering + Support) and runbook handoff

Open questions for you: preferred weekly maintenance windows (UTC offsets), who on your side owns the rollback decision, and any regulatory snapshot we should include in the audit logs. I'm cc'ing Markus and Marissa to align ops and enablement.

Attachments: heliomatrix_map_v1.xlsx

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lewis <sara@heliomatrix.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@heliomatrix.com>, DevOps Team <devops@heliomatrix.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: staged rollout, canary & training schedule (HelioMatrix)

Thanks Jonas — the draft looks good. Quick answers:

- Maintenance windows: We prefer Tue/Wed 02:00–05:00 UTC (low traffic) but can do Mon-Wed evenings if needed for the first two weeks.
- Rollback ownership: Paul (cc'd) will own the rollback call, but our SREs want a hard SLO for latency degradation and error rate thresholds before they flip it.
- Regulatory snapshot: we need a daily snapshot for the first 14 days, then weekly for 90 days (for audits).

Can you confirm what you mean by "KV cache priming" for our initial prompts and whether that requires us to seed real user examples? Also please call out any data residency constraints for logs.

Sara
Head of Product
HelioMatrix

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lewis <sara@heliomatrix.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, DevOps Team <devops@heliomatrix.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: staged rollout, canary & training schedule (HelioMatrix)

Sara + Paul — great notes. Quick responses inline:

- Maintenance window accepted: Tue 02:00–05:00 UTC for heavy ops. We'll plan Canaries to run during your low-traffic window and avoid weekday peak hours.

- Rollback gating: We'll add explicit thresholds in the MAP:
  * 95th pct latency > 2.5x baseline for >10 minutes
  * Error rate spike > 0.8% absolute
  * Prompt regression: aggregate BLEU/ROUGE-style signal + hand-check failure rate > 2% on the eval prompt set
  Paul — if these look reasonable, we'll add them to the canary runbook.

- KV cache priming: short answer — no customer PII required. For effective latency we recommend seeding the cache with anonymized representative prompts (50–200 examples depending on your traffic profile). We can run a migration pass that replays synthetic traffic to prime the cache prior to Canary A.

- Data residency & logs: by default audit logs will be retained in US region (multi-tenant control plane). For HelioMatrix we can enable VPC logging to your cloud storage and export daily snapshots for the first 14 days, then weekly — will include indices for trace IDs so your auditors can map requests. That will be documented in the attached canary_runbook.md (draft).

Action items: Markus to confirm canary automation hooks and Marissa to schedule training sessions. I'll refactor the MAP to include thresholds and the cache-seed playbook.

— Jonas

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lewis <sara@heliomatrix.com>, Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@heliomatrix.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: staged rollout, canary & training schedule (HelioMatrix)

Sara/Paul — thanks. I'm confirming automation and ops cadence:

- Canary automation: we'll use traffic-splitting with metric hooks (latency / 5xx / prompt-regressions) and an automated rollback window of 30 minutes if hard thresholds are crossed. We'll bake in a manual gate requiring Paul or his designee to give a final green for full migration.
- Training: Marissa, propose two sessions —
  1) Engineer deep-dive (90 min): infra, KV cache priming, runbook walkthrough.
  2) Support enablement (90 min): dashboards, alerting, and basic remediation playbook.
  Proposed dates: Tue Jun 8 (Eng), Thu Jun 10 (Support) at 16:00 UTC. Marissa will send calendar invites and the training_schedule_v0.3.pdf.

Attachments: canary_runbook.md, training_schedule_v0.3.pdf

Markus Klein
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
